newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: TENNIS-MUSTER DEFIES DOCTOR'S ORDERS TO PLAY ON.
newsitem.headline: TENNIS-MUSTER DEFIES DOCTOR'S ORDERS TO PLAY ON.

text.p: For most amateurs, playing tennis with an injury would be madness. For Austrian clay court master Thomas Muster, it's become a way of life.
The former French Open champion and world number one has been troubled by a recurring hip injury for 15 years, but he has vowed to play on for at least another three years against doctor's orders.

"Doctors would always advise you to take it easy, but if I had taken it easy every time a doctor tells me, I would still be ranked 600 in the world," he said on Saturday after his third round victory in the Australian Open.
Asked if he had been warned about any serious long-term effects of playing with the injury, Muster said: "If I'd listened to doctors I would have stopped 15 years ago."
Speaking to reporters after his straight sets victory over German qualifier Jens Knippschild, Muster said he accepted the risks associated with playing tennis.
"Professional tennis is not a healthy thing, you know, but we will see. So far so good," said Muster, the champion on the clay of Roland Garros in 1995.
"It is not healthy, and whatever you do on your body, your back or your hips, whatever you use to play, we know that once we get older that things start hurting," Muster said.
"We are putting a lot of strains on the body so that is the price you pay for it," said Muster, the fifth seed at Melbourne Park.
Muster, 29, was forced to retire from tournaments in Stuttgart and Paris last October with the hip problem, a lingering injury from his childhood.
